L0@P0: The Commonwealth of Massachusetts
L1@P0: William Francis Galvin, Secretary of the Commonwealth
L2@P0: Elections Division
L3@P0: One Ashburton Place, Room 1705, Boston, Massachusetts 02108 • (617) 727-2828
L4@P0: Election Advisory #26-11
L5@P0: Electioneering within 150 Feet of Voting Locations for the State Election
L6@P0: October 14, 2026
L7@P0: Under Massachusetts law, electioneering, campaigning, signature-gathering and other specific
L8@P0: political activities are prohibited within 150 feet of a voting location. The 150-foot rule applies
L9@P0: to:
L10@P0: • Polling places on Election Day
L11@P0: • Early voting sites, during voting hours
L12@P0: Enforcement of the 150-Foot Rule is the responsibility of the presiding officer of the voting
L13@P0: location. Because interpretation and enforcement of the law may depend on the discretion of
L14@P0: the presiding officer, the Elections Division is providing this Advisory to clarify what does and
L15@P0: what does not violate the law relative to campaign activity in and around voting locations.
L16@P0: Presiding officers must enforce the 150-Foot Rule according to the guidance in this Advisory,
L17@P0: and are permitted to use their discretion only on matters not explicitly prohibited or allowed by
L18@P0: this Advisory.
L19@P0: As a local election official, you must provide all presiding officers with a copy of this Advisory
L20@P0: and make it available in each voting location.
L21@P0: Citations
L22@P0: The 150-Foot Rule is contained within section 65 of chapter 54 of the Massachusetts General
L23@P0: Laws. Additional information about prohibited activity around voting locations may be found in
L24@P0: 950 CMR § 52.03(22)(c) and 54.04(22)(c).
L25@P0: Prohibitions regarding hindrance or interference with a voter may be found in section 29 of
L26@P0: chapter 56 of the General Laws. Section 46 of chapter 56 of the General Laws prohibits
L27@P0: disturbing the peace or decorum at the polls. Sections 71 and 74 of chapter 54 of the General
L28@P0: Laws authorize enforcement of the election laws by the presiding officer and police officer or
L29@P0-1: constable at the voting location. 2
L30@P1: Applicability of the 150-Foot Rule
L31@P1: The 150-Foot Rule broadly prohibits political and campaign activities in the areas in and around
L32@P1: voting locations during voting hours. The rule applies to polling places and early voting sites.
L33@P1: The application of the 150-Foot Rule is limited only to voting locations and the immediate
L34@P1: vicinity of a voting location, so as not to place an unreasonable restriction on protected political
L35@P1: speech.
L36@P1: The 150-Foot Rule does not apply to central tabulation facilities, advance ballot processing
L37@P1: locations, ballot drop-boxes, or local election offices that are not located in the same building
L38@P1: as a polling place or early voting site.
L39@P1: The 150-Foot Rule also does not apply to any event that takes place after Election Day,
L40@P1: including post-election tabulation for the State Election.
L41@P1: Prohibited Activities
L42@P1: Under state statute and regulations, a person may not do anything within 150 feet of a voting
L43@P1: location designed to aid or defeat or otherwise promote or oppose a candidate or question
L44@P1: being voted on in that location.
L45@P1: Prohibited activities include:
L46@P1: • Holding certain political signs
L47@P1: • Wearing certain political apparel (t-shirts, hats, buttons, pins, stickers, etc.)
L48@P1: • Handing out campaign literature
L49@P1: • Distributing stickers for write-in campaigns
L50@P1: • Shaking hands or otherwise greeting voters (while being a candidate on the ballot)
L51@P1: • Asking voters to vote in a certain manner
L52@P1: • Hindering or interfering with voters who are voting or on their way to vote
L53@P1: • Soliciting signatures on any type of petition – whether or not it pertains to the current
L54@P1: election
L55@P1: State law prohibits signature gathering of any kind within 150 feet of a voting location. This
L56@P1: includes state ballot question petitions, citizen’s petitions, and nomination papers.
L57@P1:  Initiative petitions and referendum petitions for the 2028 State Election are currently
L58@P1-2: circulating. Signatures on these petitions cannot be gathered within the 150-foot area.3
L59@P2: Materials are considered to influence voters if they contain:
L60@P2: • A candidate’s name
L61@P2: • The name of a candidate’s policy proposal
L62@P2: • A candidate’s slogan or image
L63@P2: • A political party name
L64@P2: Further, no person may hinder, delay, or interfere with a voter without lawful authority. This
L65@P2: includes any attempt to induce a voter to disclose how they have voted before they deposit
L66@P2: their ballot.
L67@P2: The prohibition against interfering with a voter protects voters who are voting or on their way
L68@P2: to vote, which means that it extends outside the 150-foot area around a voting location.
L69@P2: The 150-Foot Rule broadly prohibits political and campaign activities in the areas in and around
L70@P2: voting locations during voting hours. The rule applies to polling places and early voting sites.
L71@P2: Specific Examples
L72@P2: Prohibited materials for the November 3, 2026 State Election would include those printed with
L73@P2: the name or face of any candidate on the ballot in that location.
L74@P2: Slogans that are closely aligned with or actively used by candidates and campaigns are also
L75@P2: prohibited. This includes, but is not limited to materials printed with:
L76@P2: • Democrat or Democratic
L77@P2: • Republican
L78@P2: • Libertarian
L79@P2: • Socialism and Liberation
L80@P2: • “Vote Blue”
L81@P2: • “Vote Red”
L82@P2: • “Vote for ______”
L83@P2: • References to statewide ballot questions, including references to:
L84@P2: o Public records or audits
L85@P2: o The Committee for Public Counsel Services (CPCS)
L86@P2: o All-party primaries
L87@P2: o Election Day registration or same day registration
L88@P2: o Tax refunds or rebates
L89@P2: o “Nature for All”
L90@P2: o Zoning or “legalize starter homes”
L91@P2: o Marijuana
L92@P2: o Firearms or gun control
L93@P2-3: • References to any local ballot question issues4
L94@P3: Allowed Activities
L95@P3: Allowed activities include:
L96@P3: • Campaigning for a candidate or ballot question not on the ballot in that location
L97@P3: • Campaigning for a candidate or issue on the ballot in a future election
L98@P3: • Holding a sign or wearing apparel that may be “political” but not intended to aid or
L99@P3: defeat someone or something on the ballot
L100@P3: • Exit polling, if speaking to voters exiting the polling location
L101@P3: Voters may bring materials to assist them in the voting process, which may include their own
L102@P3: personal notes or checklists, as well as campaign literature that would otherwise be prohibited
L103@P3: in the polling place. These materials are allowed, as long as the voter does not display them to
L104@P3: others.
L105@P3: Poll workers must regularly sweep voting booths, to ensure campaign literature and stickers are
L106@P3: not left behind by voters.
L107@P3: Exit polling is permitted within 150 feet of a polling place on Election Day, as long as the exit
L108@P3: pollster does not interfere with a person or voter on their way to an election.
L109@P3: The display of materials, phrases, and slogans promoting an issue, position, or ideology not
L110@P3: explicitly tied to a campaign or political party on the ballot cannot be prohibited under the 150-
L111@P3: Foot Rule.
L112@P3: Specific Examples
L113@P3: Permitted materials for the November 3, 2026 State Election would include materials printed
L114@P3: with:
L115@P3: • References to President Trump that do not include the name of a political party or
L116@P3: candidate on the ballot
L117@P3: • “Make America Great Again” or MAGA, unless there is a candidate on your ballot known
L118@P3: to be using that campaign slogan on signage or campaign materials
L119@P3: • References to the importance of voting generally, without reference to voting for a
L120@P3: candidate, party, or ballot question
L121@P3: Enforcement of the 150-Foot Rule
L122@P3: The presiding officer of each voting location is responsible for enforcing the 150-Foot Rule and
L123@P3: other laws regarding the maintenance of peace, order, and decorum at the voting location.
L124@P3: Presiding officers must ensure that voting locations are unobstructed and that voters are not
L125@P3-4: hindered. 5
L126@P4: At a polling location, the presiding officer is typically the Warden, though the city or town clerk
L127@P4: may also be present and assist with enforcement. At an early voting location, the presiding
L128@P4: office is typically the local election official, but the local election official may authorize someone
L129@P4: else to act in their stead.
L130@P4: To enforce the election laws, the presiding officer may issue orders to any voter, observer,
L131@P4: election official, or other individual to comply with the laws and regulations, as described in this
L132@P4: Advisory.
L133@P4: The police officer or constable assigned to a polling place enforces the election laws at the
L134@P4: order of the presiding officer. The presiding officer may ask the police officer to take into
L135@P4: custody anyone who, by disorderly conduct, interrupts or disturbs the proceedings of the
L136@P4: election.
L137@P4: The presiding officer has significant discretion in determining what they believe amounts to a
L138@P4: disturbance to the peace, an obstruction to the polling place, or a hindrance to the voters. They
L139@P4: do not have the same discretion in determining violations of the 150-Foot Rule, as the terms
L140@P4: and definitions of the rule are clearly defined in this Advisory and in statute.
L141@P4: Presiding officers may exercise discretion in matters pertaining to the 150-Foot Rule only when
L142@P4: such matters are not provided for in this Advisory.
L143@P4: Enforcement of the 150-Foot Rule should occur in a manner that plainly and directly addresses
L144@P4: the violations of the rule, without stating or implying bias or prejudice on the part of the
L145@P4: presiding officer. Officials invoking the 150-Foot Rule must make every effort to emphasize that
L146@P4: the voter’s right to vote is not being infringed upon, and that (if applicable) the voter will be
L147@P4: allowed to vote when they comply with the law.
L148@P4: Election workers should call the local election office if they or any voter is threatened or
L149@P4: intimidated, or if a disturbance of any kind occurs.
L150@P4: If law enforcement is not present, election workers should call local law enforcement if they
L151@P4: believe the safety of any person in the voting location is in jeopardy.
L152@P4: Questions & Complaints
L153@P4: Voters, election officials, campaign officials, members of the media, and members of the public
L154@P4: may contact the Elections Divisions with any questions regarding the content of this Advisory or
L155@P4: the enforcement of the 150-Foot Rule.
L156@P4: Those who have evidence that the 150-Foot Rule has been enforced in a manner that is
L157@P4: inconsistent with this Advisory may file a complaint with the Elections Division’s Legal Counsel.
L158@P4: The Elections Division may be contacted at elections@sec.state.ma.us or (617) 727-2828.
